question: Manjit’s salary is ₹10,000 per month. He spends ₹6,000 on house rent and ₹3,000 on bills, and the rest of the amount is his monthly savings. Find his savings (in ₹) in a year, if in the month of his birthday, he spent all his monthly savings on birthday
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Monthly **Savings** = 10,000 − (6,000 + 3,000) = ₹1,000.

Total months in a year = 12.

Savings are zero for 1 month (**Birthday month**).

Total Savings = 1,000 × (12 − 1) = 1,000 × 11 = ₹11,000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/820751de9465d4459d0360aad06227d194654fce4c4f39964bdead3a9d7f5a3c.png] 

**Given:**

**Monthly Salary** = ₹10,000

**Expenditure** (Rent + Bills) = 6,000 + 3,000 = ₹9,000

**Calculations:**

⇒ Monthly Savings = Salary − Total Expenditure

⇒ Monthly Savings = 10,000 − 9,000 = ₹1,000

⇒ Number of months in a year = 12 months

⇒ Since savings of 1 month (birthday month) is spent, effective saving months = 11

⇒ Yearly Savings = 1,000 × 11

⇒ Yearly Savings = ₹11,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Basic Savings Formula

Savings = Income − Expenditure. This is the fundamental identity used in all personal finance problems.

Percentage Savings

Savings % = (Savings ÷ Income) × 100. In this case, monthly savings % = (1,000 ÷ 10,000) × 100 = 10%.

Annual Calculations

To find annual values, multiply monthly values by 12, adjusted for any special conditions (like the birthday expense here).
